reader.requirement: At --std 85 an alphabetic argument position must take an elementary item of class alphabetic (PICTURE A and B, §1985:IV.4.3.3) or a nonnumeric literal of alphabetic characters only, and may use its size; in the 1989 module every A position (LENGTH, LOWER-CASE, UPPER-CASE, MAX/MIN, ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN, REVERSE) also admits X or N, so the rule only defines admission and never alone forces a refusal.

edition-consulted.switches: sig.IntroducedIn > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel refuses a function not yet introduced (DiagnosticCatalog.IntrinsicFunctionNotYetIntroduced); the 1989 functions carry IntroducedIn 85 in IntrinsicCatalog, so --std 85 admits them
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(ctx.Edition.Edition.Year) gates each per-position predicate by its Since year; the class screen itself (IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation over Verified) is edition-blind
ConstructRegistry NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002: at --std 85 a numeric/integer function is admitted only inside an arithmetic expression (a nested function argument is one)

reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|CobolVersion|since|Std|1985|1989' over IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs and IntrinsicBinder.cs; the only edition reads on the argument path are ArgPredicate.Since/AppliesAt, sig.IntroducedIn and the 2002 placement construct; ClassOf1/ClassOfPlace/ClassOfItem/ClassOfPic/Admissible/Violation consult no edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: Admissible('s') admits class alphabetic at every edition; at 85 the national member of the set is unreachable because no national item or literal exists (N"..." refused COBOL0900)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf04_07 covers PIC A(n) items and alphabetic literals; PIC A with B insertion, alphabetic table elements with computed subscripts and ALL subscripts are not exercised

refuter.evidence: Read §1989:A.2.2 AR2 and Table 1 (A positions: LENGTH, LOWER-CASE, MAX, MIN, ORD, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, REVERSE, UPPER-CASE, each also admitting X or N), so AR2 alone never forces a refusal; the rule's only distinct effect is MAX's footnote (all-alphabetic arguments give type alphanumeric).
